title: When All Contemporary Actresses Are Younger

commenti.body:
I feel you. I've been feeling this a lot as I've travelled, and somewhat stumbled, through my twenties. We all have our dreams and seeing others have them as reality can make one envious, especially when they are younger than you, it makes one feel like they are too old to achieve them. However, we should remember that plenty of successful people didn't "make it" until they were a little older. Morgan Freeman for example, was in his late-thirties when *The Electric Company* became his big break. It wasn't until he was in his forties that he became a "star", it's never too late to pursue your dreams. 

At the same time, always remember what *you* have achieved.

> How do others navigate this dynamic? Does it serve as motivation, or does it sometimes raise questions about your own path?

You probably want to ask this in some sub for actors. Me, as someone who loves movies, that fact has no reason to motivate me at all, if anything it's a reminder that I'm getting old, but almost everything reminds you of that as you get older.

So, yes, actresses probably have always been on the young side, throughout the entire history of movies.

I think that is something everyone goes through as they age, really regardless of profession.  I remember when the realization hit that every professional athlete was younger than me, even though I was never going to be a professional athlete.  It is just a strange and somewhat jarring transition to move from looking "up" (in age) to a group of people, to looking down at them.
